label: A10-AARCH64-LINUX-BOOT-BATCH
title: Integrate AArch64 Linux boot on Catapult A10
dispatch_status: integration-owner-active; board bring-up milestone passed, Flash cold boot pending power cycle
scope: Bring the current AArch64 core to Linux userspace with JTAG-UART interaction on Catapult A10. This parent owns board SoC Timer/GIC/UART/Flash integration, system-level Linux boot simulation, serialized integration of software and loader lanes, and the minimum coherent candidate for volatile board bring-up.
writes: integration-only merge, interface resolution and evidence review

children.T-20260928-003: Linux 6.6 lite config, Catapult DTB and integer userspace init
children.T-20260928-004: Versioned AArch64 Flash payload packer, loader image and host-side format tests

validation.owner_initial: Focused timer/GIC/UART and board-top simulation as each independent interface is implemented; no full Gate D during exploration.
validation.integration: One Catapult SoC Linux boot smoke on the integrated SHA, from BRAM reset through DDR Image entry, /init marker and UART command/reply.
validation.physical: After the simulation candidate is ready, resource-locked 25 MHz Quartus physical/assembler then one authorized volatile SOF test; Flash programming is a later milestone.
validation.resource_policy: All local and GamePC heavy jobs take the matching resource-lock. Do not run parallel Quartus or Linux long simulations against a shared output root.

acceptance: Simulation shows Linux enters userspace and a UART command receives its expected response; matching candidate boots to the same milestone on the physical board before Flash cold-boot closeout.

16 MiB Linux diagnostic reached the timeout without reproducing the old page-table external abort; the observed low-memory/SWIOTLB path was not representative of the 128 MiB board.
128 MiB Linux diagnostic passed loader handoff and progressed through page-table setup into initramfs/allocator work without synchronous abort, but did not reach /init within 1.5B cycles.
GIC telemetry run ruled out repeated MMIO RWP reads at GICD_CTLR/GICC_CTLR; Linux ended with tty0 selected and the JTAG UART bootconsole disabled, while TX WSPACE remained 64.
128-byte TTBR1 4 KiB-page LDRB scan passed through the Catapult write-back D-L1/L2 coherence subsystem with a 4 KiB D-L1 set-conflict/replay sequence.

The same scan passed with production Catapult L2 geometry (256 sets x 2 ways); 4 KiB-spaced D-L1 conflicts replayed from L2 without extra PoC reads. A 64-set/1-way L2 stress variant passed and refetched the evicted lines.
A focused Catapult M1-B -> AXI4 -> 512-bit Avalon regression passed one full 64-byte DDR line, checking all eight 64-bit words and four 128-bit AXI response beats.

Core-integrated TTBR1 LDRB -> JTAG-UART CONTROL.WSPACE read -> STR W DATA loop passed 128 bytes through the Catapult write-back coherence path and production lcvex_catapult_soc_jtag_uart bridge. Each CONTROL read returned WSPACE=64; every committed store and observed TX byte matched. This focused synthetic program still does not reproduce the full Linux transcript corruption or prove userspace startup.

Root cause for the first printk NUL is a cache-line-crossing 8-byte LDP at PA 0x40670b7a; the old L1 line reader zero-filled bytes beyond the line, and its store path also dropped the corresponding final bytes.
Focused L1WB regression passes the repaired cross-line read/store path, dirty adjacent-line hit/victim, and second-line refill fault cases.
